planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Nagasaki forms an evergreen diploid clump and is one of David Kirchhoff's earlier award-winning doubles, later used as a breeding parent for other double daylilies.

directions: Bred by David Kirchhoff and registered in 1978, Nagasaki is an evergreen diploid daylily bearing fully double blooms in an ivory, cream, and pink-lavender blend with a greenish-yellow halo and green throat, about 4.5 inches across on 19-inch scapes in the early-midseason with extended bloom and rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Honorable Mention in 1982 after being named a Judges' Choice selection in 1979, and was later used by Kirchhoff as a parent of other double-flowered daylilies, including 'Cabbage Flower'. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.
